questions.stem: A profile service accepts a display name when `name.length() <= 10`. A user enters a name made of six emoji, each from outside the Basic Multilingual Plane. What does the check decide?

options.text: It rejects the name, since length() returns 12: each of these emoji takes two UTF-16 units
options.says: length() counts UTF-16 char values, and a character outside the BMP is a surrogate pair

options.text: It rejects the name, since length() returns 24: each of these emoji takes four UTF-8 bytes
options.says: a String counts UTF-16 units, not the bytes of any encoding; length() is 12

options.text: It accepts the name, since length() returns 6: it counts the characters the user sees
options.says: the user sees six characters, but length() counts twelve units

options.text: It accepts the name, since length() returns 6: Java stores each of these emoji in one char
options.says: a char is 16 bits; a character outside the BMP takes two of them

origin.section: length(), charAt() and substring() Count UTF-16 Units, So an Emoji Counts Twice

questions.stem: A log indexer reads lines of up to 2,000,000 characters, keeps `line.substring(0, 16)` of each in a long-lived map, and drops the line. On Java 21, what does each entry in the map keep in memory?

options.text: About 16 characters, since substring() gives the key an array of its own
options.says: substring copies the characters it returns, so the line can be collected

options.text: About 16 characters, since the key keeps the line's array and the GC frees the part outside it
options.says: substring gives the key an array of its own; it keeps nothing of the line's array

options.text: The whole line, since substring() shares the line's array and records an offset
options.says: that was Java 6 and early Java 7; in Java 21 the substring has its own array

options.text: The whole line, since the key keeps a reference to the String it was cut from
options.says: substring copies, so the key doesn't keep the line alive

origin.section: length(), charAt() and substring() Count UTF-16 Units, So an Emoji Counts Twice

questions.stem: A product's colours are stored as `"red,,blue,,"` and the shop counts them with `colours.split(",").length`. What count does it show?

options.text: 3, since split() drops only the empty strings that come at the end
options.says: split(regex) uses limit 0, which removes only trailing empty strings

options.text: 2, since split() drops every empty string, wherever it comes
options.says: an empty string between two matches stays; only trailing ones go

options.text: 5, since split() keeps every empty string, wherever it comes
options.says: that is split(regex, -1); the one-argument form drops the trailing ones

options.text: 4, since split() drops only the one empty string that comes last
options.says: limit 0 removes every trailing empty string, not just one

origin.section: split() Takes a Regex and Drops Trailing Empty Strings

questions.stem: A required field is checked with `value.strip().isEmpty()`. A user pastes into it a single U+00A0 copied from a web page. What does the check decide?

options.text: It treats the field as filled in, since strip() keeps U+00A0: Character.isWhitespace excludes it
options.says: strip() uses Character.isWhitespace, which excludes the no-break space

options.text: It treats the field as filled in, since strip() keeps U+00A0: it removes only characters up to U+0020
options.says: removing chars up to U+0020 is trim(); strip() removes Unicode whitespace such as U+2003

options.text: It treats the field as empty, since strip() removes U+00A0: Character.isWhitespace includes it
options.says: Character.isWhitespace excludes the no-break space U+00A0, so strip() keeps it

options.text: It treats the field as empty, since strip() removes U+00A0: it removes every character up to U+00A0
options.says: removing every char up to a limit is what trim() does, with U+0020 as its limit

origin.section: trim() Stops at U+0020, strip() at Unicode Whitespace, and Neither Removes a No-Break Space

questions.stem: A billing mail is built with `body.replaceAll("\\{total\\}", total)`, and for one customer `total` is `"$7.00"`. What happens?

options.text: It throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, since the second argument refers to a group the pattern lacks
options.says: in a replacement, $7 means group 7 of the match, and the pattern has no groups

options.text: It throws PatternSyntaxException, since the first argument has a brace that starts a repetition
options.says: the braces are escaped, so the pattern is valid; it is the replacement that fails

options.text: It inserts $7.00, since only the first argument of replaceAll() is interpreted
options.says: the replacement is interpreted too: $ and \ have meanings there

options.text: It inserts .00, since the group the second argument refers to matched nothing
options.says: a group that doesn't exist is an error, not an empty string

origin.section: replace() Replaces Every Literal Match; replaceAll() Interprets Both of Its Arguments
